# Open questions

Points where the ECMS Technical Specification v1.0 and the ECMS User Stories v3b are ambiguous or disagree. The components do not take a position on any of them: they display what the backend sends. Each item names what is waiting on an answer.

## Ambiguities that affect the interface

| # | Question | Where | What waits on it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Valuation factor direction.** Factors are labelled "EC/kWh", but every story divides by them (30 kWh at 0.9 → 33 EC = 30 ÷ 0.9; 250 kWh at 1.1 → 227 EC = 250 ÷ 1.1). Read that way, "higher-value" injection factors (1.1, 1.2) earn *fewer* credits, which contradicts the narrative. Story 5 mixes both readings. | Stories 1–2, 5, 8, 15–17 | Any display of factors or formulas. `EnergySummary` shows kWh and credits only. |
| 2 | **How members authorise a transfer.** Wallets hold `private_credentials` used to authorise operations, with device-, cloud- or ECMS-hosted options, but the member's signing step is not described. | Spec 4.2.1–4.2.2 | Whether `TransferForm` needs a signing step. It currently reports only `working`, `done` or `error`. |
| 3 | **Minimum guaranteed balance and transfers.** The safeguard stops *consumption deductions* below a minimum; it is not stated whether P2P transfers or settlement requests may go below it. | Spec 4.4.2, 8.3 | `TransferForm` and `SettlementRequestForm` check only against the `available` figure the backend sends. |
| 4 | **Purpose code for P2P transfers.** A P2P request includes a `purpose_code`, but no code fits a gift between members, and stories record P2P transfers without one. | Spec 9.2; Stories 4, 7, 13 | `TransferForm` does not ask for a purpose. |
| 5 | **Which wallet receives a transfer** when the recipient holds several wallets. | Spec 4.2.2, 7.1 | `RecipientPicker` lists the entries the backend supplies (`id` is the receiving wallet). |
| 6 | **What members may see of each other.** Members access only their own data (RBAC), yet choosing a recipient needs names. Pseudonyms apply to the ledger; the member directory is not addressed. | Spec 8.2 | `RecipientPicker` shows whatever `name` and `detail` the backend provides. |
| 7 | **Presenting a negative member balance.** Financed assets leave members at, e.g., −20,000 EC (Story 15). How to explain this to members is not defined. | Stories 15–17 | `WalletBalance` shows the minus sign in normal text and an optional `negativeNote` from the backend. No wording is proposed. |
| 8 | **Reserve Wallet.** Listed as a wallet type, but the `wallet_type` enum is only MEMBER, COMMUNITY, DEPENDENT. | Spec 4.2.2 vs 4.2.4 | `AccountList` and `AccountCard` label only the three enum values. |
| 9 | **Settlement request states.** A request is forwarded for CEMA approval, but its states (sent, approved, rejected) and how the member is told are not defined. | Spec 4.8, 9.3 | `SettlementRequestForm` only confirms the request was sent. No request-status component yet. |
| 10 | **Error codes.** Only `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` is named. Limit, eligibility and suspended-member errors have no codes. | Spec 9.2 | Components show a generic message for any other code. |
| 11 | **Euro value of credits for settlement.** Either computed by a rule in Component C or confirmed manually by the CEMA. | Spec 9.3 | `SettlementRequestForm` shows an estimate only if the backend supplies one. |

## Inconsistencies in the documents

| # | Issue | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | Story 9's community wallet should end at −10,019 EC (−9,953 + 214 − 30 − 250), not −9,917. | Story 9 key data |
| 13 | Story 21 uses an M2D (member-to-dependent) transaction, which is not in the `tx_type` enum. | Story 21 vs spec 7.2 |
| 14 | The reading-roadmap table (phases 1–7) does not match the phase headers in the body (phases 1–8, different story ranges). | User stories, section 4 |
| 15 | CEMA is expanded two ways: "Community Energy Management Authority" and "Energy Community Management and Administration Entity". | Spec 1.5 vs glossary |
| 16 | The glossary lists a Component D (Member & Asset Registry Interface) that the architecture table does not include. | Spec glossary vs 4.1 |
| 17 | Section numbering restarts or jumps (e.g. 1.1 inside section 2, 6.2.1 inside 4.2, two section 8s). | Spec |

## Wording to check with members

The plain-language labels in `PurposeTag` ("Solar energy you shared", "Community energy you used", "Support from the community" and so on) and the member flows' sentences are proposals. They have not been tested with members.
